title: Transcutaneous Auricular Vagus Nerve Stimulation as an Augmentation Method for Psychosomatic Multimodal Treatment: A Randomized Controlled Study
summary:
The goal of this study is to investigate the effectiveness of a treatment using a neuromodulator. This device sends targeted electrical impulses to the brain through the vagus nerve. This method is called transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation (tVNS). It helps reduce pain and improve mental well-being. Patients who suffer from somatoform disorders and/or trauma-related disorders, and are currently undergoing inpatient treatment at the University Hospital for Psychosomatic Medicine and Psychotherapy at Otto-von-Guericke University Magdeburg in Germany, are eligible to participate.

Participants will use the device to carry out two stimulations per day, each lasting at 60 minutes. The strength of the electrical pulse is set on the device to a level just below the individual discomfort threshold.

A total of 90 patients will be studied, divided into three groups. Thirty patients will undergo the actual treatment, thirty will receive a placebo treatment (inactive tVNS device), and thirty will receive standard care without the tVNS intervention. Data will be collected at three time points: before the intervention, after completion of the intervention (after 4 weeks), and three months after the intervention.

Following completion of the intervention, semi-structured interviews will be conducted with a subsample of participants.

interventions.name: Intervention group receiving active transcutaneous vagus nerve stimulation (tVNS) as an augmentation strategy to a multimodal psychosomatic-psychotherapeutic complex treatment (duration: 6–12 weeks), with two stimulations per day, each lasting 60 minutes.

Control group receiving a sham intervention during a multimodal psychosomatic-psychotherapeutic complex treatment (duration: 6–12 weeks), involving two sham stimulations per day using an inactive device, each lasting 60 minutes.
Control group receiving standard multimodal psychosomatic-psychotherapeutic complex treatment (duration: 6-12 weeks) without additional intervention (treatment as usual, TAU).

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
ICD-10 Diagnosis F45.-
Adults aged 18 and older who are undergoing inpatient treatment for a somatoform disorder (F45.-)
Written consent
Fluent knowledge of German
Exclusion criteria:
Severe psychiatric disorder according to ICD-10 (F00-F09, F20-F29, substance use disorders)
Pain or injuries in or around the ears
Implanted pacemaker
Acute risk of harm to self or others
Inability to provide consent
